sources.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Maxwell’s Equations: Continuous and Discrete, ETH Research Report 2015-18
sources.locator: Complete 56-page report fetched and inspected. §§3.1–3.3, printed pp. 23–26 (PDF pp. 24–27): oriented finite meshes, cochains, signed incidence matrices, Theorem 7, and the scope of cochain sampling.

contents.name: §§3.1–3.2, Definitions 4–6: oriented cells, finite cochains, relative orientation and incidence matrices
contents.support: The definition states the finite coordinate spaces, map shapes, dual-coordinate conventions and zero-composition hypotheses explicitly; signed incidence matrices are one admissible realization.

contents.name: §3.2.2, Theorem 7: the successive discrete exterior derivatives compose to zero
contents.support: This source states D_{k+1}D_k=0 for incidence cochains. The local proof applies the two identities directly to the finite update.

contents.name: §3.2.2, Theorem 8: cochain potentials under trivial-topology hypotheses
contents.reason: The assigned model admits general finite complexes and proves no potential-existence or topology-classification result.

contents.name: §3.3, equations (42)–(44): sampled continuum Maxwell fields satisfy exact cochain equations
contents.reason: The items do not construct sampling maps from continuum solutions and make no continuum-consistency or convergence claim.

sources.title: Davit Harutyunyan, Adaptive Vector Finite Element Methods for the Maxwell Equations, University of Twente dissertation (2007)
sources.locator: Complete 210-page dissertation fetched and inspected. Ch. 6, §§6.4–6.9, printed pp. 161–174 (PDF pp. 171–184): bounded-domain Maxwell conventions, positive variational forms, finite-element matrices, leapfrog time stepping, and discrete-divergence constructions.

contents.name: §§6.5–6.7, equations (6.26)–(6.45): positive material forms and finite-element mass matrices
contents.support: This is a concrete finite-element realization of positive mass matrices. The assigned definition permits arbitrary symmetric positive maps and does not import its material law, boundary conditions or Whitney spaces.

contents.name: §6.8, equations (6.54)–(6.56): staggered leapfrog, a matrix-dependent CFL condition and a discrete energy
contents.support: The section gives a related finite-element time scheme. The assigned algorithm specifies its own cochain update in exact rational arithmetic and does not import the thesis scheme or its stability proof.

contents.name: §6.8, equations (6.54)–(6.56): exact energy conservation for the stated source-free finite-element scheme
contents.support: This is recorded as an independent comparison only; the assigned semidiscrete and staggered invariants are derived directly for the stated matrices and update.

contents.name: §6.9, equations (6.57)–(6.64): divergence-free magnetic flux from a discrete de Rham sequence
contents.support: The thesis uses a Whitney finite-element reconstruction with an initially divergence-free field and, for its electric constraint discussion, rho=0. Our proof instead propagates the two abstract algebraic constraints from D_2D_1=D_1D_0=0.

contents.name: §6.9, discussion after equation (6.64): loss of order and lack of convergence for one first-order Whitney postprocessing
contents.reason: The assigned items contain no mesh family, approximation theorem or convergence conclusion.
